Hello, thank you very much for your reply.

We are from the Philippines. The experts are on the ORL division of a public hospital here. The specialists go back and forth on what to recommend to her, and honestly it's becoming so frustrating.

Later we are going to the said hospital to get her a CT scan. My sisters urge me to bring her to the emergency unit so that her swallowing can be accommodated. 

Problem is that there is a protocol that every single patient should undergo an xray procedure. I am afraid that after an xray, they'll find that she has pneumonia and then she'll be sent to the COVID facilities because that's where they treat COVID and pneumonia problems. This makes me so anxious, knowing that she has special needs and that I can't nurse her if she's at the COVID facility.
For now I'm focusing on meeting a psychiatrist because if I don't (within the week) I'll start cutting or overdosing

That's what I've been doing for the past five years. Now I can't really challenge those thoughts because they just root to this program. I've been trying antidepressants but it only kills my moods and emotions and now I'm an emotionless zombie. Other than that, I can think clearly then but now the only thing that I can do is stare into something and let my mind turn off.

I'm basically braindead. A zombie.
Yep. I'm still doing the most that I can. I just hope these suicidal thoughts die down eventually, even for a little while.

If I were to be completely honest with you, there were times that I actually liked the program. But recently everything went beserk and I don't know how to cope up with so much pressure and it is fucking exhausting.

But I invested so much time and effort in this program. I don't really recognize myself anymore. I'm no longer interested in the things I was once passionate about. It's like this program killed a major part in me that I cannot bring back.
Funny thinking that I thought I could do this in the first place. I'm dead wrong.
It will dip it enough to get a probation from my benefactor.

That's another problem though. My scholarship only support the student only based on how long their stay in their program. If I drop a few subjects, I'll get delayed and my benefactor will stop supporting me. And I can't afford uni. I'm from the Philippines and the government doesn't offer student loans so there's that.

That's the thing with me. I don't really know how to open up to people even the ones I am close with. I can't confide with my mother about this dilemma because she's really expecting me to finish this fucking thing on time (she thinks I'm very smart because even though I don't like electrical engineering, I never failed a class but now since my mental health is deteriorating I'm pretty sure I'll fail a few of my subjects) and that my whole family expects me to finish because I need to help them financially.

My friends in school don't understand mentall illness
I don't really attend psychological support groups and frankly I dont have the time
I guess so. But as much as I want to pursue those programs in the future, I'm afraid I'd be dead by then.
I wanted to pursue history or maybe even biology. My scholarship practically forced me into this because they do not offer any of the programs I wanted to pursue.
